text.insert: Review the game's standards after initial knowledge base seeding and before starting Run. Use the seeded code evidence and source captures to identify missing requirements or rules that need revision. The baseline standards review still happens before backfill so librarians can recognize existing authored rules.
Separate Shared Rules From Game Requirements

A rule belongs in the shared set only when it applies across games. Keep requirements tied to one game's upstream conventions, compiler behavior, or source layout specific to that game. Review any proposed global change against the other games that depend on it.
Global and Game Scope

defines the proposed scope model. Automatic composition of shared and game-specific rules is not implemented, and override behavior remains undecided. Game-specific storage alone does not establish either behavior.
Review and Author the Rules

steps.text: Confirm the selected game and resolved source path. Read accepted rules alongside upstream requirements and the seeded knowledge.
Write the requirement, preferred and rejected forms, and intended applicability. Keep unreviewed additions proposed.
Provide a concrete bad example and repair. Associate existing lint rule IDs where available, or state the required human review.
Resolve conflicts with existing rules and assess effects on other games before changing a shared requirement.
Check worker instructions, librarian recognition context, and QA behavior against the reviewed rules. Record any scope or enforcement gaps explicitly.

text.insert: Standard Record
supplies the field definitions, JSON examples, status values, and family file layout. Use that contract when editing the configured
decomp_standards
source.
The standards service reads and edits the source resolved for the selected game. Inspect the returned game and source path before saving changes.
GET /api/standards
exposes records, examples, effective prompt XML, recognition context, and warnings.
POST /api/standards
applies a validated record edit. These endpoints do not implement a shared-plus-game scope resolver.
Verify the Rule Is Applied
An accepted record does not create a lint check. Confirm that each declared
qa_rule_ids

entry names an implemented check and that the bad example produces the expected finding. Check that the preferred repair passes. For requirements without automated checks, name the review mechanism before relying on them.

When a project slice requires build evidence, test both the source finding and the post-scan gate. SMS requires fresh objects and upstream symbol-map validation for changed game C++ sources; a patch-only scan cannot pass that gate. Record heuristic naming and padding coverage separately from human evidence review. Verify the selected standards and shared scanner reach the deployed worker environment before treating host tests as worker readiness.
Worker Enforcement
describes prompt inclusion and QA checks. Librarians use standards for recognition and do not create or change them through semantic proposals.

Finish this review with the configured rules, examples, and enforcement understood for the selected game. If a requirement depends on the proposed scope resolver, keep that dependency visible instead of treating it as active. Revisit affected knowledge if a rule change alters how a librarian should interpret an observed code pattern.
